label: copy-phase input token b
explanation: Fires whenever the copy-phase input (the fed-back previous output) is the letter b: at step t > L with in_tok = b, i.e. right after the model has emitted b. Dev precision is 1.0 (every copy-phase b input activates it) and recall is 0.93, covering 98.6% of the activation mass. Magnitude stays fairly uniform (median about 0.75 of max) and is unaffected by copy position, L, or which token comes next. It peaks when b immediately follows another b or the delimiter. It does not fire on b during the original phase, apart from rare weak activations (about 0.1-0.2 of max) at original steps 1-2; these make up most of the misses. It does not fire on other tokens, on the delimiter, or on outputting b when the input is something else.

issues: Minor: the predicate misses weak original-phase b activations. (in_tok==b)&(phase==0) fires 4.5% of the time, holds 1.1% of the mass, and all of it sits in the bottom activation quartile. Most of it is at orig_idx 1-2 (2738 and 1297 active steps), with a small tail at idx 3-8. This matches the explanation's 'rare weak activations' claim and is too weak to justify adding a term.

The other misses are scattered weak firings (about 0.10-0.14 of max) on non-b tokens (z, j, 0, k, ...; each roughly 0.1% rate or less). There is no anticipatory pattern: next_out==b with in_tok!=b gives precision 0.0008.

Claims checked: test precision 1.000, recall 0.933, F1 0.965, mass recall 0.986 reproduced. No false positives on test. Copy-phase rate is flat at about 0.034 across recall_idx and L. Precision of in_tok==b alone is 0.483, which matches the stated 0.48. Copy-phase b preceded by b has precision 1.0 and is over-represented in the top activation quartile, which supports the 'highest on b after b' claim.
